summary: Instagram is doing most of the work: nearly every Hindi video there gets 1,000+ views, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best videos are early ones (late Oct to early Nov) about a sensor that 'doesn't do the obvious thing' (clap switch, gyro robot, IR robot), and the very newest videos (Nov 16-20) are falling to 140-360 views, so something has slipped. Saves and shares are rare, but a few videos (soil sensor, IR robot) got strong shares even with low views, which shows the idea works when people see it.
winningPattern: A relatable robot or clap-switch/sensor-based gadget, shown with a 'it doesn't do X, it only does Y' or 'without this, the robot fails' hook in Hinglish, with a short curiosity title and an emoji (🤖 👏 🎤 🔥), posted on Instagram first. Videos that show a visible, funny behaviour (robot falling, clap/whistle triggering) beat pure explainers like 'How does X work?'. Titles that name the myth plus the surprise ('Taali nahi, sirf shor sunta hai') perform best, and YouTube only works when the video also has a clear, searchable topic like clap switch, PIR or gyro.
doMore: Lead with a robot or a clap-switch style demo where something visibly goes wrong or surprises, then explain why
Use the 'X doesn't do the obvious thing, it only does Y' title, but keep it to one short sentence
Make follow-ups to the winners: gyro robot part 2, clap switch with whistle or noise, line follower, mic vs speaker
Reuse the topic of each Instagram hit on YouTube with a searchable title, since YouTube views are tiny for most uploads
Add a closing question or 'save this for your project' line to lift saves and shares
Check why the last 10 videos dropped (Nov 11-20) and compare their first 2 seconds with the Oct 29-Nov 5 hits
stopDoing: Plain 'How does X work?' titles for everyday items (mall door, street light, smartwatch, TV remote)
Posting niche component videos (TDS meter, geyser thermocouple, KY-038) back to back, as they get the lowest reach
Posting videos to YouTube only, with no Instagram version, as those get almost no views
